title: ROW_NUMBER
description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (...) assigns a unique, sequential integer to each row based on an ordering, without collapsing rows the way GROUP BY would. Write a query that returns every product's `name`, `price`, and a sequential rank starting at 1 for the most expensive product.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: ROW_NUMBER, window function
ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price DESC) computes a running row count in price order WITHOUT grouping the other columns away - every product still gets its own row, just with a number attached.
Select name, price, and a ROW_NUMBER() window function ordered by price descending, from products.
expected_behavior: Returns name, price, and a 1-based rank per product, most expensive first.
solution: SELECT name, price, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_rank FROM products;
explanation: A window function runs "over" a set of rows related to the current one (here, ALL rows, ordered by price) without merging them into fewer rows - that's the key difference from GROUP BY, which does merge rows.
